places.name: Hacienda Flores
places.note: The outfit finds a small herd of stolen Wilbarger horses, then Call, Pea and Newt run off a hundred-plus Flores horses past the sleeping hacienda.
places.location_hint: northern Mexico south of the Rio Grande opposite Lonesome Dove; the main horse herd grazed a mile from headquarters, the smaller herd in a valley south of an old line camp

places.name: Mexico
places.note: Jake grumbles about riding across it; Newt fears that horse stealing there could get him hanged.

places.name: Rio Grande
places.note: At sunrise Call waits on its bank as the big stolen herd drinks and then crosses to the north side.

places.name: Comanche crossing near Lonesome Dove
places.note: Newt recognizes the river bend here at dawn and knows he is nearly home; the herd crosses into Texas.
places.location_hint: on the Rio Grande about a mile upriver from Lonesome Dove

places.name: Chaparral plain south of the Rio Grande
places.note: Near a dense thicket the outfit's herd collides with one being run south by Mexican horsethieves, causing a stampede.
places.location_hint: in Mexico, a short way south of the Rio Grande near Lonesome Dove, on the route back from the Flores ranch

places.name: Lonesome Dove
places.note: Destination for both stolen herds; Newt imagines riding in with the horses and being seen as a man.
places.location_hint: south Texas border town on the north bank of the Rio Grande, about a mile below the old Comanche crossing

places.name: Texas
places.note: The captured horses are mostly Texas stock; Newt notes horse stealing is a hanging crime on the Texas side.

places.name: Galveston
places.note: Where the two lost Irishmen had been trying to go.

places.name: Ireland
places.note: Augustus jokes about how far off course travellers from there have strayed.

places.name: Montana
places.note: Call plans to take surplus horses there; Newt tries to imagine its buffalo, mountains and snow.

places.name: Kansas
places.note: Most Lonesome Dove cowboys going north only reach it, which they think far.

places.name: Arkansas
places.note: Augustus teases that Jake is used to its whores and feather pillows.

groups.label: Call's detail
groups.hint: crossing the Rio Grande at sunrise with over a hundred horses, about a mile above Lonesome Dove

groups.label: Wilbarger horse drovers
groups.hint: driving about forty recovered Wilbarger horses back toward Lonesome Dove; position at dawn not stated

groups.label: Augustus and the Irishmen
groups.hint: rode off with two horses to fetch the stranded Irishmen and follow the herd home
